edition.en: Poems of Gerard Manley Hopkins (1918), edited by Robert Bridges, from the scan-backed transcription on Wikisource; the editor’s notes omitted
edition.zh: 据维基文库依扫描本校录的《霍普金斯诗集》（1918），罗伯特·布里奇斯编；略去编者注

basis.en: Written in 1877 and first published in 1918; the author died in 1889 and the editor in 1930.
basis.zh: 1877 年写成，1918 年首次出版；作者卒于 1889 年，编者卒于 1930 年。

note.en: The octave describes a world worn smooth by trade and toil; the sestet answers that “nature is never spent”, and the freshness is still “deep down things”. Read it aloud: Hopkins wrote for the ear, and the repeated “have trod, have trod, have trod” is meant to be heard.
note.zh: 前八行写一个被买卖与劳作磨平的世界；后六行回答说“自然永不枯竭”，那份清新仍在“万物深处”。请读出声来：霍普金斯为耳朵写作，那反复的“踩过，踩过，踩过”是要被听见的。

excerpt.orig:
And for all this, nature is never spent;
There lives the dearest freshness deep down things;
excerpt.en:
And for all this, nature is never spent;
There lives the dearest freshness deep down things;
excerpt.zh:
尽管这样，自然永不枯竭；
在万物深处，住着最珍贵的清新；

note.en: An octave of a world smeared by trade and a sestet that answers it with freshness deep down things; Hopkins’s music at its most controlled.
note.zh: 八行写被劳作与买卖弄脏的世界，六行以万物深处的清新作答；霍普金斯的音乐在这里最为收放自如。
